The entire 10-second video is rendered as a refined animated graphite drawing with monochrome black, soft gray, and white values. The pale-blue costume is represented with very light cool-gray graphite shading and a subtle restrained blue-gray tint, while the floral embroidery remains visible through fine pencil details. Avoid photorealism, glossy 3D rendering, anime cel shading, or a fully colored realistic look.

Her long black hair and translucent sleeves are lifted by the breeze. She begins with a poised classical Chinese dance stance: one foot grounded, the other stepping lightly forward, one arm curved above her head and the other extended diagonally outward. The camera makes a subtle forward push-in. Loose graphite motion lines around her sleeves and hair establish the energetic hand-drawn style.

She performs two light traveling steps through the forest, pivots smoothly, then makes a controlled half-turn. Her long skirt arcs outward in a clean circular sweep, and the translucent sleeves trail behind her arms. Her upper body remains graceful and upright while her footwork is quick and precise. Use expressive curved pencil strokes to emphasize the direction of her spin, fabric movement, and flowing hair. Keep her face, hairstyle, costume silhouette, and body proportions stable across frames.

Her arms open like unfolding ribbons, then cross briefly in front of her torso before extending outward again. The forest trunks slide gently in parallax behind her. The graphite animation should show subtle successive sketch traces around her hands, feet, hair, and sleeves, suggesting speed without creating confusing duplicate limbs. Her movement is beautiful, disciplined, and expressive, inspired by classical Chinese dance rather than martial arts.

[Shot 4: 00:07.000-00:09.000]
The camera arcs around <Subject 1> in a smooth semicircle from front three-quarter view to side view. She executes a fast elegant spin with one leg extended low and the skirt flaring in a broad crescent. Her head turns slightly after the body, creating a graceful delayed follow-through. Fine pencil hatching defines the folds of the dress, while energetic loose contour lines accent the sleeve tips and hair strands. The mist and tree branches remain soft and sparse, preserving generous white negative space.

[Shot 5: 00:09.000-00:10.000]
The movement resolves into a final classical Chinese dance pose. <Subject 1> finishes facing slightly toward the camera, one arm extended upward and the other curved near her waist, with one foot pointed lightly behind her. Her hair and sleeves continue to settle for a moment after the final turn. The camera ends on a medium full-body frame with a subtle push-in. The last image is a clean, elegant graphite illustration with a few lingering pencil motion lines fading into the white mist. End without a hard cut, morphing, facial distortion, extra limbs, or loss of costume details.
